note:
This transaction is the first chunk of the McDougall Litecoin v1 executable trapezoid specimen. It was confirmed on September 5, 2026 at 8:43:30 p.m. MDT (September 6 at 02:43:30 UTC).

The experiment preserved a small runnable program across Litecoin OP_RETURN records so a browser could reconstruct it from ledger data. This was part of the McDougall/M64 artifact resurrection work, including the broader goal of recovering artifacts when their ordinary hosted or IPFS copies disappear.

This record contains the first 80 raw token bytes at locator 3172893:13. Byte values above 0x7f refer to the McDougall dictionary; for example, 0x86 expands to "function". The payload is therefore binary tokenized JavaScript. Rendering it as UTF-8 produces broken characters; Base64 is only another representation of those bytes.

The earlier continuation at 3172924:19 stores 38 ASCII hex characters. The corrected canonical root at 3172942:28 stores the same payload directly as 19 binary bytes: version 01, a four-byte pointer back to 3172893:13, and the final 14 program bytes. Either continuation reassembles the same 94-byte stream, which hydrates to 194 bytes of JavaScript drawing a filled trapezoid on a canvas.

The published JSON records were reconstructed and matched against the original repository protocol note and recovered September 6 conversation. A fresh independent explorer check returned HTTP 403 during this analysis; the locator positions are retained from the original receipts and protocol notes. The existing tools/mcdougallResolver page reconstructs the program with its fixed dictionary and keeps execution behind a separate RUN button.
